context: Parallel coordinates chart showing 300 employee records across 6 mixed-scale axes (2 linear, 1 log, 2 ordinal point, 1 linear) colored by 6 departments using a TOL colorblind-safe palette, with per-axis brush filtering.
first_impression: Technically well-executed but the ordinal axes (Department, Education) create dense fan convergence zones that dominate the visual field and make unfiltered exploration difficult.
what_works: The 6-color TOL palette is perceptually distinct and the legend is immediately legible; canvas rendering at 0.30 opacity with two-pass dimming on brush is a smart approach that manages 300-line density on the continuous axes.
what_doesnt: The two ordinal axes bottleneck all 300 lines into 5–6 discrete y-positions, producing thick overlapping bundles that obscure trajectory patterns until brushing is applied; the visualization depends heavily on interaction to be readable, which is a perceptual risk for first-time viewers who haven't brushed yet.
